target_customer: Urban Indian consumers seeking therapy and psychiatry consultations, who pay fees comparable to in-person visits
problem: Access to doctors and therapists in India is hard to navigate and logistics heavy. DocVita runs consultations over Zoom, Google Meet and WhatsApp with a concierge who handles scheduling and back office work.
business_model: Consumer healthcare marketplace and clinic: fee per consultation, with a take from provider fees
product_category: Telehealth and online mental health clinic

founders.name: Anmol Arora
founders.background_notes: From the YC page, which cites marketing and product led growth expertise. Search summaries mention a predecessor company, Chota Hospital Private Limited, from corporate records not opened here.

competitors.name: Wysa
competitors.what: Mental health support app named in 2020 coverage of Indian mental health startups

competitors.name: InnerHour
competitors.what: Online therapy and self-care platform named in 2020 coverage of Indian mental health startups

technical_complexity.rationale: Consultations run on off the shelf video tools and WhatsApp with operations done by a concierge team, so the engineering is light.

defensibility.rationale: Telehealth booking over WhatsApp was easy to copy and many Indian telehealth and mental health startups existed. Provider relationships are the only slight barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Practo and Lybrate were general telemedicine platforms in 2020. No incumbent acquired DocVita and no copy of its WhatsApp model was documented.

market_need_then: COVID-19 lockdowns in 2020 pushed Indian consumers toward telemedicine and mental health helplines. Traxcn data cited in coverage says Indian mental health startups raised about 20M USD between 2016 and 2020.

identity.logo: A plain letter D mark per a directory listing
identity.visual_style: simple healthcare look with WhatsApp access emphasized
identity.voice_and_tone: friendly, made with love in India

branding.brand_signature: Care delivered inside a single WhatsApp chat with no app to install

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. The name is a doctor and life Latin blend resembling other health brands, and sources do not explain it.

pivots.from: General telehealth and earlier hospital software
pivots.why: A directory summary says Arora's own search for a therapist drove the change; the company site now describes an online clinic for therapists and psychiatrists.

outcome_analysis: DocVita is a small Bengaluru telehealth company that narrowed from general consultations to therapy and psychiatry delivered over WhatsApp. Its public funding is limited to unverified aggregator figures of roughly 125K to 130K USD, so it looks like a slow-growing, capital light business rather than a venture scale raise. It is listed as active with about 14 people and no shutdown, sale or layoffs were found, and its stalling relative to VC backed peers is inferred.
notes: YC lists the batch as Winter 2020; the shard says Summer 2020. Unverified funding: Persana says 125K USD across 2 rounds (pre-seed 2021-10) and CB Insights says 130K USD over 4 rounds with a Seed II on 2022-03-15 from Flat6Labs Ignite. Both are aggregators and no round is recorded. The competitor article could not be opened (HTTP 403), so the Wysa and InnerHour entries rely on a search summary that said they were named in 2020 coverage. Founding date conflicts: 2019 on YC, 2015 predecessor in corporate records, 2021 elsewhere.
